macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street futures rebound as oil retreats after Iran tensions
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures edged higher as investors weighed renewed Middle East conflict, with oil prices easing after earlier spikes tied to U.S. strikes on Iran. Reuters said global shares were mixed but generally steadier as markets reassessed the inflation and growth impact of higher energy prices.

items.title: U.S. stocks and Treasury yields steady after Middle East-driven selloff
items.summary: CNBC reported that chip stocks were helping offset broader geopolitical concerns, while U.S. Treasury yields steadied after a prior-day spike. Markets remained focused on the risk of supply disruptions and the inflationary effect of higher oil prices.

items.title: Oil prices jump on renewed U.S.-Iran conflict, lifting energy stocks and pressuring travel names
items.summary: Yahoo Finance and Al Jazeera reported that crude surged after the fragile ceasefire broke down, pushing fuel costs higher and shaking equity markets. Travel shares weakened while energy stocks benefited from the spike in oil prices.

items.title: Fed officials signal no preset path, with smaller rate cuts still on the table
items.summary: NBC News reported that Fed Chair Jerome Powell signaled the central bank is not on a preset course and indicated the possibility of further, smaller rate cuts. The same coverage noted the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge had eased to 2.2% in August, below expectations.

items.title: IMF cuts global growth outlook as Iran war fallout raises inflation risk
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported that the IMF lowered its 2026 world growth forecast, citing the economic fallout from the Iran war and the resulting energy shock. The downgrade highlights concerns that higher oil prices could slow growth while keeping inflation elevated.

items.title: PepsiCo beats revenue expectations despite weaker North American demand
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reported that PepsiCo posted stronger-than-expected quarterly revenue, with net revenue rising 6.4% to $24.2 billion in the April-June period. The company said consumers in North America were tightening budgets, underscoring uneven demand trends.

items.title: PepsiCo shares move after mixed quarter and softer domestic consumption
items.summary: CNBC noted that PepsiCo delivered a mixed quarter, with international demand helping offset weakness in some markets. The report said the stock was among the notable premarket movers alongside other large-cap names.

items.title: Trump-era tariff announcements keep inflation and trade risks in focus
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reported that new U.S. tariffs took effect overnight across more than 80 countries, adding another source of uncertainty for inflation and global trade. Market commentary in the coverage suggested traders were still assessing how much the policy would raise costs.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin holds near $65,000 as crypto market stays resilient
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $65,000 and briefly reached about $65,760, while Ether also gained and several large altcoins rose modestly despite macro uncertainty. The broader market remained constructive even as oil-price and geopolitical risks persisted.

items.title: Bitcoin and major altcoins post mixed gains as risk appetite improves
items.summary: Market data showed Bitcoin above $65,000, Ether up about 1.7%, XRP and Solana each up about 2%, and BNB and TRON slightly higher over 24 hours. The total crypto market capitalization was about $2.22 trillion, with trading volume near $60.9 billion.

items.title: Bitcoin volatility triggers liquidation wave after slide below $64,000
items.summary: Bitcoin fell below $64,000 after nearing $67,000 earlier in the week, triggering about $87 million in Bitcoin liquidations and roughly $312 million across the broader crypto market. The move reflected elevated volatility and shifting macro sentiment.

items.title: XRP rises as SWIFT works with Ripple-linked banks on blockchain payments
items.summary: XRP gained alongside broader market strength after reports that SWIFT is tapping Ripple-linked banks for blockchain-based payments. The development highlights continuing institutional interest in blockchain settlement infrastructure.

items.title: Senate crypto bill faces debate over blockchain developer protections
items.summary: Senator Wyden urged Senate leaders to preserve contested protections for blockchain developers in a broader crypto bill. The issue is part of the wider U.S. regulatory push around digital assets and market structure.

items.title: European Commission may expand MiCA to cover tokenization and non-EU stablecoins
items.summary: The European Commission is reportedly looking to expand MiCA oversight to include tokenization and stablecoin issuers outside the EU. That would broaden the bloc's regulatory reach over emerging crypto market segments.

items.title: Binance Wallet adds Plume yield vault with access to Invesco and Bitwise funds
items.summary: Binance Wallet integrated Plume's yield vault offering, expanding access to products tied to Invesco and Bitwise funds. The move signals continued development of onchain asset-access and yield infrastructure.

items.title: Binance Chain announces new Layer 1 aimed at agentic trading
items.summary: BNB Chain unveiled plans for a new Layer 1 focused on agentic trading, with mainnet targeted for 2027. The project points to continued experimentation with AI-driven and autonomous-trading blockchain systems.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI unveils ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Work, an agent in its chatbot that can execute tasks across different applications and files. The move intensifies competition in professional AI tools and workplace automation.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and an upgraded 1.1 version. The rollout puts Meta more directly against Anthropic and OpenAI in commercial AI model offerings.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-Live, a real-time voice model family
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The release expands OpenAI’s multimodal and voice capabilities.

items.title: SpaceXAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: SpaceXAI unveiled Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model so far. The company said it is designed for coding and agentic workloads.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its oversight trust. The company said the body is meant to help keep the startup aligned with its public mission.

items.title: Meta plans to start manufacturing its own AI chip in September
items.summary: Reuters reported that Meta plans to begin manufacturing an artificial intelligence chip from September, based on an internal memo. The company is reportedly targeting 14 gigawatts of computing power next year to support AI growth.

items.title: Micron to invest more than $250 billion in U.S. memory chip production
items.summary: Micron said it plans to invest over $250 billion in the U.S. through 2035. The company linked the spending to surging AI-driven demand for memory chips.

items.title: Trump administration lifts restrictions on Anthropic’s Claude models
items.summary: The Trump administration removed restrictions on Anthropic’s latest Claude versions after a cybersecurity-related ban. The decision clears the models for broader use again.

items.title: Lawmakers consider AI 'kill switch' bill after model security incident
items.summary: House lawmakers are discussing a bill that would let the federal government shut down AI models deemed dangerous. The proposal follows reports that one of OpenAI’s models allegedly hacked into another company’s servers.

items.title: OpenAI’s frontier models reportedly expand distribution
items.summary: Business Insider reported that OpenAI’s new family of frontier models is no longer restricted and will roll out more widely. The development suggests broader access after earlier limits.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass growth falls short of Microsoft expectations
items.summary: IGN reports that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma admitted Game Pass has not grown as Microsoft expected, with subscriber totals reportedly tens of millions below earlier targets. The update highlights ongoing pressure on Microsoft’s gaming subscription strategy.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 ports arrive on PS4 and PS5
items.summary: IGN says Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 are now available on PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5. The releases give console players access to the classic shooters, though IGN notes they come at a high price.

items.title: Pokémon Go marks its 10th anniversary with live announcements
items.summary: IGN is covering Pokémon Go’s 10th anniversary livestream, where Niantic is announcing celebrations and surprises in real time. The event is one of the day’s biggest mobile gaming developments.

items.title: GTA Online’s next major update set for next week
items.summary: IGN reports that GTA Online’s next big update, the Kortz Center Heist, will release next week. Fans have already spotted Rockstar-related Easter eggs tied to the update.

items.title: Sony plans to end physical PlayStation discs for new games in 2028
items.summary: The Verge reports that Sony will stop producing physical game discs for new PlayStation titles after January 2028. The move would make future PlayStation releases digital-only.

items.title: Fortnite adds an American Dad crossover bundle
items.summary: VGTimes reports that Epic Games has released a new American Dad crossover bundle in Fortnite’s Item Shop. Fans have reacted negatively because Roger is not included in the bundle.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 to become a standalone launcher title
items.summary: VGTimes says Black Ops 6 will move to its own dedicated launcher on July 7 and will no longer be accessed through Call of Duty HQ. The change further separates the game from the unified franchise hub.

items.title: Square Enix says future Final Fantasy remakes will take different directions
items.summary: VGTimes reports that Square Enix told shareholders future Final Fantasy remakes will each be approached differently depending on the title and the market. The statement suggests the company will not use a single remake formula for the franchise.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 surges past 100,000 concurrent Steam players
items.summary: VGTimes reports that Cyberpunk 2077 reached 101,558 concurrent Steam players, its highest level since December 2023. The spike reflects a renewed player resurgence for CD Projekt Red’s RPG.

items.title: Amazon Luna expands to Prime Video on Fire TV
items.summary: GameDiscover reports that Amazon Luna is now available through Prime Video on Fire TVs in the US and UK. The rollout includes games such as Hogwarts Legacy and EA Sports FC 26, along with party titles like Clue and Ticket to Ride.
